title: introduce-ci-dryrun-standardize-action-inputs-and-cache-eviction-policy
author: Aisha Kapoor
description: Motivation: developers waste time iterating on CI workflows because reproducing GitHub Actions locally is slow and caches accumulate stale entries. This PR introduces a lightweight 'ci-dryrun' shim for local validation, standardizes Action inputs across repo workflows to reduce copy/paste and surprises, and adds a conservative cache-eviction policy + an automated pruning Action to reclaim buildup. High-level summary of changes and rollout: 1) ci-dryrun: a small CLI wrapper (tools/ci/dryrun) that validates workflow inputs, runs a fast smoke execution using containerless steps (node/go shims), and verifies cache-key calculations without network access. Intended for local dev and CI maintainers. 2) Action input standardization: reworked most .github/workflows/*.yml to accept a single standardized inputs file .github/ci/inputs.yml and added a reusable composite action .github/actions/inputs-guard to verify presence and types. 3) Cache eviction policy: added scripts/scripts/cache-evict.sh and a scheduled workflow .github/workflows/cache-prune.yml that prunes caches older than 30 days but keeps recent builds; eviction policy is conservative to avoid perf regressions. 4) Dep pinning helper: a small tool tools/dep/pin-checker that warns about floating devDeps and recommends lockfile updates; hooked into PR lint. 5) Docs and onboarding: docs/dev/ci.md and tools/ci/dryrun/README.md with examples and failure modes. Compatibility and safety: default behavior is opt-in via labels; scheduled cache pruning is limited to non-shared caches used only by CI jobs. Rollback: scheduled workflow is disabled behind a feature flag (repo setting) and can be reverted by flipping .github/ci/flags.yml. Testing: ran full CI on this branch, smoke-tested ci-dryrun on macOS/Linux, ran scheduled prune on a small sandbox org. Impact: faster developer iteration, fewer accidental cache misses, and a plan to keep cache growth in check. Follow-ups: a separate PR will add metrics to Console for cache reclaim and per-run cache hit ratios.
